slot.brief: Lens immersed in a medium of given refractive index; use lens-maker relation to find new focal length and nature of lens

stem: A thin converging lens of refractive index $1.60$ has power $+5.0\ \text{D}$ in air. It is immersed in a liquid of refractive index $1.20$. What are its focal length and nature?

verdicts.working: Lens power in a medium scales by \(\frac{n_\text{lens}/n_\text{medium}-1}{n_\text{lens}-1}\). Thus \(P_\text{liquid}=5\times\frac{1.6/1.2-1}{1.6-1}=25/9\,\text{D}\), so \(f=1/P=+0.36\,\text{m}=+36\,\text{cm}\).

working:
$$P_m=P_a\dfrac{\dfrac{n_l}{n_m}-1}{n_l-1}=5.0\dfrac{\dfrac{1.60}{1.20}-1}{1.60-1}=\dfrac{25}{9}\ \text{D}$$
$$f_m=\dfrac{1}{P_m}=\dfrac{9}{25}\ \text{m}=+36\ \text{cm}$$
Positive focal length: converging.

Independent check: Lens power in a medium scales by \(\frac{n_\text{lens}/n_\text{medium}-1}{n_\text{lens}-1}\). Thus \(P_\text{liquid}=5\times\frac{1.6/1.2-1}{1.6-1}=25/9\,\text{D}\), so \(f=1/P=+0.36\,\text{m}=+36\,\text{cm}\).
solution:
The power of a lens in a medium is $P_m=P_a\dfrac{(n_l/n_m)-1}{n_l-1}$.
$$P_m=5.0\dfrac{(1.60/1.20)-1}{1.60-1}=\frac{25}{9}\,\text{D},\qquad f_m=\frac{1}{P_m}=+0.36\,\text{m}=+36\,\text{cm}$$
Since the focal length is positive, the lens remains converging.
